root_cause: The TF2 Keras LSTM test 'test_keras_lstm_flags_float32' fails with a max diff of 0.117 against the default tolerance of 5e-2 (0.05). The test exercises LSTM with relu activation, tanh recurrent_activation, dropout=(0.1, 0.3), use_bias=False, and 'flags=True'. With dropout enabled in inference mode ('flags=True'), slight weight/gate interactions lead to floating-point accumulation differences between OpenVINO CPU inference and the TF reference. The same test with the same parameters also failed on 2026-06-29 (max diff 0.052) in a Linux run (investigation 2026-06-29-12-11-47-000-28161192347.json), confirming this is a pre-existing flaky numerical behaviour. The PR being tested (#36640) adds CI Doctor JSON schema files only and does not touch any LSTM, TF frontend, or CPU plugin code.
recommended_actions: Re-run the merge queue to confirm flakiness — the same test failed on 2026-06-29 with a smaller diff (0.052) on Linux
Investigate LSTM relu+dropout CPU implementation for non-deterministic numerical precision accumulation
Consider widening the tolerance for this specific LSTM configuration (relu + dropout + no bias) from 5e-2 to 1.5e-1 or mark as xfail with a tracking issue
Review whether 'flags=True' inadvertently enables training-mode dropout during inference, causing different numeric paths
prevention_strategies: Track LSTM numerical tolerance failures in a dedicated test skip config. If the test consistently flakes beyond 5e-2 tolerance, raise the epsilon for non-deterministic LSTM configurations or add an xfail marker with a tracking ticket.
historical_context: Prior occurrence on 2026-06-29 (investigation 2026-06-29-12-11-47-000-28161192347.json): Linux run 28161192347, same test/params, max diff 0.052, marked Medium confidence. PR #36640 does not modify LSTM/TF-related code.
